title: Introduction to New Features in the Latest CLO 7.1
description: The latest version CLO 7.1 has been officially released. CLO experts demonstrate over 40 new features—watch now! Let’s master CLO 7.1 together~
transcript:
Hello everyone, I am Stella from Cloud Shanghai.  
Today, my colleague Familia and I will introduce the new features of version 7.1.  
This time, our new features are divided into 8 parts.  
These are the main updates: 3D function, 2D function, virtual model, process details, rendering, text editor, and other files.  
Now let's take a look at the main update content.  

The first update is the seamless text editor.  
This update has added the seamless text editor.  
You can use the scanned image to generate continuous text in all directions.  
You can also check the effect in the 3D window.  
There are two modes, automatic mode and manual mode.  
Next, let's learn how to use this function.  

First, let's go to the object window.  
Find the object.  
On the right side, you can see that a plus button has been added.  
Hover the mouse over the top.  
You can see that the seamless text editor is created.  
Open the text editor.  
The window of the text editor will appear in the 2D window.  

Next, I will introduce the structure of the text editor window.  
First, it is divided into two windows.  
The upper part is the editing window of the object text area.  
The lower part is the preview window of the result.  
We will press the button at the bottom left to open the original text.  
You can see the original text image in the top editing window.  
The scroll wheel can be used to adjust the size of the text.  
At the top, you can see the size and resolution of the sample.  
The maximum size that can be supported at the moment is 9999 pixels by 9999 pixels.  
If the original image is larger than this value, it will be automatically reduced to 9999.  
So please make sure that the size of the original image is smaller than the upper limit value.  

We can see the material ball on the upper left.  
Click to switch to check.  
Because this image was created before loading,  
the system will automatically detect the found image and import it.  
This is the secret rule of the picture.  
Pictures that need to be imported together must use the same name as the original text.  
In addition, the system can detect these pictures only by using the English underscore and the corresponding suffix.  
For example, the suffix of the found image is _Normal or _NRM.  
The other material pictures are the same.  

Next, let's introduce the automatic mode.  
First, select the physical area.  
We find the smallest area where the texture pattern repeats.  
When choosing, it should be larger than this area.  
Then press the left mouse button to drag and select.  
The selected area is recommended to be larger than 200x200 pixels.  
After the selection is complete, small blue grids will appear within the frame selection range.  
This is the single cycle range selected after automatic analysis.  
In the window below, it will display the results of the automatic analysis of the selected area.  
The scroll mouse wheel can enlarge and shrink the texture pattern.  
When you open the grid button in the window, you can identify the original location of the area through the grid lines.  
You can check the clothing effect in the 3D window.  

For example, if you want to adjust the area, you can drag and select again.  
Or move to select the point of the area.  
After adjustment, you will automatically analyze and generate the results in the selected area again.  
In the lower right corner of the selected area, you can see the icon of the automatic mode.  
You can see the automatic mode description on the top of the icon.  
The selected area will automatically adjust to the best result.  

In the automatic mode, you can set the top right corner of the texture type and the average option.  
Choosing the texture type is to get a more accurate analysis result.  
And because the texture type is based on the line chart,  
it still needs to be in the line chart in order to generate the result.  
You can see that the small triangle of the texture type has pure color, duplicate, and random.  
Pure color refers to the pure color of the texture without a pattern.  
Duplicate refers to the texture pattern with a rule.  
Random refers to the texture pattern without a rule.  
Adjusting the average value can be used to average the difference in brightness caused by fold marks on the texture.  

The button on the far right is the smooth button.  
If the original image is not scanned evenly,  
or the linking part of the repeated image is not smooth due to fold marks,  
the automatic adjustment result may not be very good.  
In this case, opening the smooth can evenly match the image.  
You can see that the image we just drew has some uneven areas.  
We open the smooth and the image is evenly matched.  

After introducing the automatic mode,  
now let's introduce the manual mode.  
I'm going to open a grid material now.  
When the part of the repetition of the texture is relatively clear,  
you can also use the manual mode when choosing the texture area.  
This is the single-cycle size of our frame selection.  
It's similar to the peek-and-seek function in Photoshop.  
The left-click drags the frame to select the smallest cycle of this pattern.  

It is still in the automatic mode.  
Because the automatic mode is the default mode.  
You can click the button at the bottom right of the selected area  
to change the mode to manual mode to keep the selected area.  
The manual mode is a small hand-shaped icon.  
After switching to manual mode,  
you need to re-adjust the selected area.  
The preview window at the bottom will update the new selection range  
and generate four consecutive repetition effects.  

If you look at the preview effect at the bottom,  
and it doesn't seem ideal,  
you can continue to adjust the area.  
Let's move to the selected area to adjust it closely.  
After the selection is complete,  
it also generates four consecutive repetition effects in the preview window.  

After editing the text,  
we can click the save button at the bottom to save.  
If it matches multiple texts,  
you can click on the selection in the preview window.  
You can save multiple texts at a time.  
Then click OK.  
After the selection is complete,  
you can confirm it.  
You can enter the name of the file.  
Click save.  

If you want to use the completed image for the object  
and use it immediately,  
you can click on apply at the bottom and close it.  
The texture will be applied to the object that was selected at the beginning,  
and the texture generator will be turned off at the same time.  

Before that,  
we needed to use other software to generate a seamless texture.  
Now you can easily generate a seamless texture in Cloud.  

Next, I will introduce another optimization for you.  
In the new version 7.1,

It can help us arrange the panels around the model quickly.  

First, we have already added a virtual model.  
Now we will add a single size.

we need to set the panel to a symmetrical state.  
Now we will set the panel to a symmetrical state.

chunks.title: Introduction to New Features in the Latest CLO 7.1
chunks.content: # Introduction to New Features in CLO 7.1 This document details the key new features, technical updates, and optimizations in CLO version 7.1. It covers improvements in the seamless text editor, 3D and 2D functions, virtual models, process enhancements, rendering, text editing, and file management, providing step-by-step instructions, technical specifications, and operational guidelines. --- ## Seamless Text Editor This section explains the new seamless text editor feature in CLO 7.1, which enables generating continuous textures from scanned images with both automatic and manual modes, supporting large image sizes and previewing effects in 3D. ### Overview and Access - The seamless text editor allows creation of continuous textures in all directions using scanned images. - Accessible via the Object Window: a new plus button appears beside objects to open the text editor in the 2D window. - The editor window is divided into two parts: - Upper: editing window showing the original text image. - Lower: preview window displaying the generated results. ### Supported Image Specifications - Maximum supported image size is 9999 x 9999 pixels. - Images larger than this are automatically resized to this maximum. - Material images linked to the original texture must share the same filename with English underscores and suffixes like `_Normal` or `_NRM` for system detection. ### Automatic Mode - Select the smallest physical area where the texture pattern repeats; recommended selection size is at least 200x200 pixels. - Drag with the left mouse button to select the area, which is then analyzed to display single-cycle texture grids. - The preview window shows the automatic analysis results and allows zooming with the mouse wheel. - Grid lines can be toggled to identify the original texture location. - Texture type options: - **Pure Color**: texture without pattern. - **Duplicate**: regular pattern texture. - **Random**: irregular pattern texture. - Average option adjusts brightness variations caused by folds. - Smooth button corrects uneven scanned images or fold mark artifacts by smoothing the texture link. ### Manual Mode - Activated by switching from automatic mode via a button in the lower right corner. - Used when texture repetition is clear, allowing precise selection of the smallest repetitive pattern. - The selection frame can be dragged and adjusted to refine the texture cycle. - The preview window updates with four repeated patterns to visualize the effect. - Supports multi-selection and saving multiple textures at once. ### Saving and Applying Textures - After editing, textures can be saved with a custom filename. - The "Apply" button applies the texture directly to the selected object and closes the editor. - This eliminates the previous need to use external software for seamless texture generation. --- ## Automatic 3D Arrangement and Panel Symmetry This section covers the new automatic 3D arrangement tool for quickly positioning panels around a virtual model, emphasizing the importance of symmetrical panel setup for accurate results. ### Setup and Use - Add a virtual model and set the panel to a symmetrical state before arrangement.
chunks.content_description: The latest version CLO 7.1 has been officially released. CLO experts demonstrate over 40 new features—watch now! Let’s master CLO 7.1 together~

chunks.title: Introduction to New Features in the Latest CLO 7.1
chunks.content: - The "Apply" button applies the texture directly to the selected object and closes the editor. - This eliminates the previous need to use external software for seamless texture generation. --- ## Automatic 3D Arrangement and Panel Symmetry This section covers the new automatic 3D arrangement tool for quickly positioning panels around a virtual model, emphasizing the importance of symmetrical panel setup for accurate results. ### Setup and Use - Add a virtual model and set the panel to a symmetrical state before arrangement. - The automatic 3D arrangement button is located in the lower-left corner of the 3D window toolbar. - Clicking it initiates dynamic panel placement based on learned data from extensive panel samples. - The arrangement process visually segments panels by color and transparency. - Users can step through each arrangement stage with back and forth buttons. - After auto-arrangement, manual adjustment is possible for misaligned panels, such as those on the back of the arm. - Manual positioning uses arrangement points to fine-tune panel placement. --- ## Automatic Conversion to CLO Action Files This feature facilitates converting external platform animation files (FBX) into CLO's action file format (MPN), enabling integration across CLO virtual models. ### Conversion Process 1. Select the virtual model in the main menu. 2. Choose "Automatically Convert to Action" and enter animation mode. 3. Select the model gender for conversion. 4. Load the FBX file via the file folder button (ensure path and filename are fully in English). 5. Click Convert and save the resulting action file. 6. The converted action file is saved by default under the virtual model file library as an MPN file. 7. Confirm and name the file (e.g., "work"). ### Integration and Usage - Action and posture files (MPN format) can be applied to all CLO models regardless of gender. - To apply, double-click the model, select the MPN action or posture file, and confirm. - The virtual model editor has been improved for easier access and operation. --- ## Virtual Model Editor Enhancements The virtual model editor has significant UI and functional upgrades to improve body shape editing and ease of use. ### Editor Versions and Interface - Three editor modes: Full Body, Body Shape, and Details. - Body Shape version added with enhanced UI grouping for upper body, lower body, and other data. - At the top, users can switch preset sizes based on different standards. - Reset, open, and save buttons are conveniently located at the back. ### Weight and Body Shape Adjustments - Full Body section includes a weight input option affecting model body shape objectively. - Example: Changing model weight from 50kg to 60kg visibly alters the virtual model. - Ideal for scenarios where only height and weight data are known. - In Details mode, a new "Simple" option combines width and weight for automatic calculation of unentered body data. - Gray data fields indicate non-editable parameters.

chunks.title: Introduction to New Features in the Latest CLO 7.1
chunks.content: - Reset, open, and save buttons are conveniently located at the back. ### Weight and Body Shape Adjustments - Full Body section includes a weight input option affecting model body shape objectively. - Example: Changing model weight from 50kg to 60kg visibly alters the virtual model. - Ideal for scenarios where only height and weight data are known. - In Details mode, a new "Simple" option combines width and weight for automatic calculation of unentered body data. - Gray data fields indicate non-editable parameters. ### Model Viewing and Simulation - Model display moved from occupying the entire window to the main menu column editor. - Allows simultaneous comparison of clothing across different sizes alongside the 2D window. - Toolbar orientation changed from horizontal to vertical. - Size adjustments (e.g., increasing total size by 100mm) update the 3D simulation in real time. - Batch updates of sizes enabled via a big update button. --- ## OBJ Zipper Function CLO 7.1 adds support for realistic OBJ zippers, expanding customization options beyond default fabric zippers. ### Features - Six preset zipper types: paper, metal, nylon, invisible, fabric (default), and OBJ. - Users can convert existing fabric zippers to OBJ type. - OBJ zippers support different materials; metal presets can be selected and color-modified. - Separate selection and editing of zipper components (zipper body, top, bottom, pull chain) are possible. - Material properties and colors can be edited in the attribute editor. --- ## Component Column in Object Window A new component column helps manage clothing components like buttons and rings more efficiently. ### Usage - Components are grouped by type and displayed with a butterfly icon in the object window. - The component column shows all components in a scene, consolidating similar parts. - Users can select components directly to modify material and color properties collectively. - Component information and structure are editable in the attribute editor. - The material list editor integrates components for easier material cost calculation and management. --- ## Clothing Roll Function This feature simplifies creating rolled clothing parts like sleeves and collars with adjustable parameters. ### Procedure 1. Select the clothing part (e.g., sleeve). 2. Use the edit sheet tool to select the outer edge(s) of the roll. 3. Right-click and choose "Roll." 4. Enter the number of roll times (max 3) and roll distance (e.g., 35mm). 5. The 3D window shows the rolled effect. 6. Thickness and tightness parameters of the sleeve chest are automatically updated to simulate firmness. 7. Further adjustments can refine the roll effect. 8. The rolled sleeve can be copied and matched for the opposite side. --- ## 3D Function Optimizations ### 3D Shape Line Tool - Allows precise dimension input for editing shape lines by right-clicking. - Supports movements such as lengthening or shortening panels with positive or negative values. - Users must enter negative values when shrinking and positive when enlarging panels. ### 3D Sewing Line Improvements - Addresses uneven thickness of sewing lines on thick-fitting garments.

Seam B is the outer seam. - Sewing line strength and thickness can be adjusted for balanced and symmetrical visual effects. ### Side Seam Parameterized Version Creation - Allows real-time preview of parameter changes in the 2D window. - Parameters such as front panel width and shoulder width dynamically update on the model. - Supports saving and loading parameter sets in CSV format for Excel editing. - Automatically arranges parameterized versions on models post-creation. --- ## Code Optimization and Editing ### Virtual Model Size Adjustment - The size of virtual model AVS can now be adjusted directly within CLO. - Procedure: - Access object window, select code, and click "Match Virtual Model." - Switch costume code to M or L. - Use "Match 3D Model" and choose to increase virtual model size. - Select appropriate AVS file from library and apply. - Automatic wearing assigns the costume to the adjusted model size. ### Code Information Display and Editing - Code group information is viewable in the attribute editor. - Users can switch between different codes within a group. - Multiple codes can be edited simultaneously by holding Shift. - Editing tools support batch modifications and outline page edits. ### POM Measurement Line Updates - POM measurement lines no longer display redundant hints. - Measurement points can cross panel gaps. - Waist and other clothing circle measurements are supported with automatic throat gap elimination. - Measurement lines update dynamically when editing outlines. - Supports selecting measurement orientation (X-axis or Y-axis). --- ## 2D Function Updates ### Split Curve Function - Enables precise addition of curve points according to selected options. -

markdown_content: # Introduction to New Features in CLO 7.1 This document details the key new features, technical updates, and optimizations in CLO version 7.1. It covers improvements in the seamless text editor, 3D and 2D functions, virtual models, process enhancements, rendering, text editing, and file management, providing step-by-step instructions, technical specifications, and operational guidelines. --- ## Seamless Text Editor This section explains the new seamless text editor feature in CLO 7.1, which enables generating continuous textures from scanned images with both automatic and manual modes, supporting large image sizes and previewing effects in 3D. ### Overview and Access - The seamless text editor allows creation of continuous textures in all directions using scanned images. - Accessible via the Object Window: a new plus button appears beside objects to open the text editor in the 2D window. - The editor window is divided into two parts: - Upper: editing window showing the original text image. - Lower: preview window displaying the generated results. ### Supported Image Specifications - Maximum supported image size is 9999 x 9999 pixels. - Images larger than this are automatically resized to this maximum. - Material images linked to the original texture must share the same filename with English underscores and suffixes like `_Normal` or `_NRM` for system detection. ### Automatic Mode - Select the smallest physical area where the texture pattern repeats; recommended selection size is at least 200x200 pixels. - Drag with the left mouse button to select the area, which is then analyzed to display single-cycle texture grids. - The preview window shows the automatic analysis results and allows zooming with the mouse wheel. - Grid lines can be toggled to identify the original texture location. - Texture type options: - **Pure Color**: texture without pattern. - **Duplicate**: regular pattern texture. - **Random**: irregular pattern texture. - Average option adjusts brightness variations caused by folds. - Smooth button corrects uneven scanned images or fold mark artifacts by smoothing the texture link. ### Manual Mode - Activated by switching from automatic mode via a button in the lower right corner. - Used when texture repetition is clear, allowing precise selection of the smallest repetitive pattern. - The selection frame can be dragged and adjusted to refine the texture cycle. - The preview window updates with four repeated patterns to visualize the effect. - Supports multi-selection and saving multiple textures at once. ### Saving and Applying Textures - After editing, textures can be saved with a custom filename. - The "Apply" button applies the texture directly to the selected object and closes the editor. - This eliminates the previous need to use external software for seamless texture generation. --- ## Automatic 3D Arrangement and Panel Symmetry This section covers the new automatic 3D arrangement tool for quickly positioning panels around a virtual model, emphasizing the importance of symmetrical panel setup for accurate results. ### Setup and Use - Add a virtual model and set the panel to a symmetrical state before arrangement. - The automatic 3D arrangement button is located in the lower-left corner of the 3D window toolbar. - Clicking it initiates dynamic panel placement based on learned data from extensive panel samples. - The arrangement process visually segments panels by color and transparency. - Users can step through each arrangement stage with back and forth buttons. - After auto-arrangement, manual adjustment is possible for misaligned panels, such as those on the back of the arm. - Manual positioning uses arrangement points to fine-tune panel placement. --- ## Automatic Conversion to CLO Action Files This feature facilitates converting external platform animation files (FBX) into CLO's action file format (MPN), enabling integration across CLO virtual models. ### Conversion Process 1. Select the virtual model in the main menu. 2. Choose "Automatically Convert to Action" and enter animation mode. 3. Select the model gender for conversion. 4. Load the FBX file via the file folder button (ensure path and filename are fully in English). 5. Click Convert and save the resulting action file. 6. The converted action file is saved by default under the virtual model file library as an MPN file. 7. Confirm and name the file (e.g., "work"). ### Integration and Usage - Action and posture files (MPN format) can be applied to all CLO models regardless of gender. - To apply, double-click the model, select the MPN action or posture file, and confirm. - The virtual model editor has been improved for easier access and operation. --- ## Virtual Model Editor Enhancements The virtual model editor has significant UI and functional upgrades to improve body shape editing and ease of use. ### Editor Versions and Interface - Three editor modes: Full Body, Body Shape, and Details. - Body Shape version added with enhanced UI grouping for upper body, lower body, and other data. - At the top, users can switch preset sizes based on different standards. - Reset, open, and save buttons are conveniently located at the back. ### Weight and Body Shape Adjustments - Full Body section includes a weight input option affecting model body shape objectively. - Example: Changing model weight from 50kg to 60kg visibly alters the virtual model. - Ideal for scenarios where only height and weight data are known. - In Details mode, a new "Simple" option combines width and weight for automatic calculation of unentered body data. - Gray data fields indicate non-editable parameters. ### Model Viewing and Simulation - Model display moved from occupying the entire window to the main menu column editor. - Allows simultaneous comparison of clothing across different sizes alongside the 2D window. - Toolbar orientation changed from horizontal to vertical. - Size adjustments (e.g., increasing total size by 100mm) update the 3D simulation in real time. - Batch updates of sizes enabled via a big update button. --- ## OBJ Zipper Function CLO 7.1 adds support for realistic OBJ zippers, expanding customization options beyond default fabric zippers. ### Features - Six preset zipper types: paper, metal, nylon, invisible, fabric (default), and OBJ. - Users can convert existing fabric zippers to OBJ type. - OBJ zippers support different materials; metal presets can be selected and color-modified. - Separate selection and editing of zipper components (zipper body, top, bottom, pull chain) are possible. - Material properties and colors can be edited in the attribute editor. --- ## Component Column in Object Window A new component column helps manage clothing components like buttons and rings more efficiently. ### Usage - Components are grouped by type and displayed with a butterfly icon in the object window. - The component column shows all components in a scene, consolidating similar parts. - Users can select components directly to modify material and color properties collectively. - Component information and structure are editable in the attribute editor. - The material list editor integrates components for easier material cost calculation and management. --- ## Clothing Roll Function This feature simplifies creating rolled clothing parts like sleeves and collars with adjustable parameters. ### Procedure 1. Select the clothing part (e.g., sleeve). 2. Use the edit sheet tool to select the outer edge(s) of the roll. 3. Right-click and choose "Roll." 4. Enter the number of roll times (max 3) and roll distance (e.g., 35mm). 5. The 3D window shows the rolled effect. 6. Thickness and tightness parameters of the sleeve chest are automatically updated to simulate firmness. 7. Further adjustments can refine the roll effect. 8. The rolled sleeve can be copied and matched for the opposite side. --- ## 3D Function Optimizations ### 3D Shape Line Tool - Allows precise dimension input for editing shape lines by right-clicking. - Supports movements such as lengthening or shortening panels with positive or negative values. - Users must enter negative values when shrinking and positive when enlarging panels. ### 3D Sewing Line Improvements - Addresses uneven thickness of sewing lines on thick-fitting garments. - Switching between Seam A (default) and Seam B shows different seam thickness effects. - Seam A is the inner seam; Seam B is the outer seam. - Sewing line strength and thickness can be adjusted for balanced and symmetrical visual effects. ### Side Seam Parameterized Version Creation - Allows real-time preview of parameter changes in the 2D window. - Parameters such as front panel width and shoulder width dynamically update on the model. - Supports saving and loading parameter sets in CSV format for Excel editing. - Automatically arranges parameterized versions on models post-creation. --- ## Code Optimization and Editing ### Virtual Model Size Adjustment - The size of virtual model AVS can now be adjusted directly within CLO. - Procedure: - Access object window, select code, and click "Match Virtual Model." - Switch costume code to M or L. - Use "Match 3D Model" and choose to increase virtual model size. - Select appropriate AVS file from library and apply. - Automatic wearing assigns the costume to the adjusted model size. ### Code Information Display and Editing - Code group information is viewable in the attribute editor. - Users can switch between different codes within a group. - Multiple codes can be edited simultaneously by holding Shift. - Editing tools support batch modifications and outline page edits. ### POM Measurement Line Updates - POM measurement lines no longer display redundant hints. - Measurement points can cross panel gaps. - Waist and other clothing circle measurements are supported with automatic throat gap elimination. - Measurement lines update dynamically when editing outlines. - Supports selecting measurement orientation (X-axis or Y-axis). --- ## 2D Function Updates ### Split Curve Function - Enables precise addition of curve points according to selected options. -
